tier_reason: README Performance table gives first-party round-trip numbers (~30 ns vs ~2 us swapcontext, ~83 us condvar thread handoff) on an i5-7200U under WSL2 with gcc 13.3 -O2, but the switch-cost benchmark code is not in the repo (only src/main.c demo and callgrind tools), so not A.

corrections.claimed_speedup: About 30 ns round trip vs about 2 us for ucontext swapcontext (~70x, README) and about 83 us for two kernel threads handing off via a condition variable (~2700x); README notes WSL2 inflates syscall costs for both alternatives.
corrections.caveats: The README does not mention Boost.Context or libco at all (the earlier caveat claiming it says so was wrong); it compares only against swapcontext, which does a sigprocmask syscall per switch, and a kernel-thread handoff, both inflated by WSL2. The switch-cost benchmark source is not published in the repo. A 30 ns round trip is likely slower than Boost.Context or minicoro-class switches (not measured here). x86-64 System V only, fixed 64 KB stacks, no scheduler yet. GPL-3.0. Tiny project (1 star, 11 commits). Off-baseline entry.

notes: Metadata from github.com pages (gh api blocked): 1 star, GPL-3.0 LICENSE text confirmed, last commit 2026-09-18. Numbers match README.

tier_reason: Upgrade from D: the README graphs (images/graph_w1.png, graph_w2.png, coros_graphs_13.png, coros_graphs_14.png) are readable plots of time in ms vs thread count against oneTBB, libgomp and libomp, and benchmark code is public in benchmarks/ (coros_fib.h, openmp_fib.h, tbb/, main.cpp); compiler, flags and CPU model are not stated, so C.

corrections.baseline: Intel oneTBB and OpenMP task runtimes (GCC libgomp, LLVM libomp); libfork is not in the graphs
corrections.claimed_speedup: Values read from README graphs (derived from page data): Fibonacci(30) x86 at 16 threads Coros ~27 ms vs oneTBB ~25 ms (parity), libomp ~140 ms, libgomp ~3000 ms; Fibonacci ARM at 16 threads Coros ~22 ms vs oneTBB ~27 ms, libomp ~85 ms, libgomp ~5000 ms; matrix multiplication x86 at 16 threads Coros ~818 ms vs oneTBB ~840 ms, libomp ~860 ms, libgomp ~900 ms.
corrections.workload: Fork-join task parallelism with C++20/23 coroutines: Fibonacci(30) task-spawn overhead and matrix multiplication, 1-16 threads, on unnamed x86 and ARM machines.
corrections.caveats: Results are graphs only, read by eye; compiler, flags and CPU models are not stated. Roughly ties oneTBB on x86 (slightly slower at some thread counts) and beats it modestly on ARM; large wins only over OpenMP tasks, especially libgomp. Requires C++23 std::expected (GCC 13+, Clang 17+). Task-parallelism library, only loosely coroutines-fibers. Stale since 2024-09-13.
